svg.text: Why redistributing the Q intensity LOWERS the 620–630 anchor — and FLATTENS the baseline through it
one dominant Q origin, at the very edge of what we capture
the same intensity split across four bands, spread to the blue
the fitted baseline — slope nearly FLAT
The far window sits on a FLANK, not on a peak, so its height reports the height of the nearest band — not the total pigment.
Measured: A(620–630) − A(520–540) = 0.0804 green vs 0.0488 brown (1.65×), over the 95.0 nm between the window centroids — 8.46 vs 5.14 × 10⁻⁴ A/nm,
which is §5.3’s fitted 8.56 / 5.22 to within 1 %. Schematic: pigment bands only, no turbidity pedestal, so its own contrast (17×) is far larger than the measured 1.65×.
⚠ The NEAR anchor is turbidity-dominated in reality, and the two classes nearly coincide there (0.1231 green vs 0.1038 brown), so the real
pair of lines pivots about a common left foot. This model has no pedestal, so its left feet differ — read the RIGHT ends against each other.
